title: backend-skeleton framework-neutral handles plan
description: Validates the output of a handles provider's plan(). Top-level and resource objects both allow additionalProperties: true so each provider can carry its own extra fields (Java: service/fetchOperation; Python: publicModel/modelImport/fetchRoute/sessionDep) alongside the neutral subset the CLI renderer and dispatch layer consume. See D-handles-providers in DECISIONS.md.

idFieldType.description: D-write-safety-phase1 (item 4a): java-spring only -- the primary key's declared Java type (e.g. 'UUID', 'Integer'). null when it couldn't be determined at all (not the same as a confirmed non-UUID type).

idFieldIsUuid.description: D-write-safety-phase1 (item 4a): mirrors typescript-express's own already-established field of the same name. false means a resolver is structurally impossible for this entity (the handles subsystem is UUID-addressable only), independent of whether a service file can be found.

requiredAuthorityForPatch.description: O5 (D-resolver-authorization-action-aware): java-spring only -- derived independently from the entity's UPDATE endpoint, not copied from requiredAuthority (which is fetch/recover's own value).

policies.description: D-resolver-policy-contract (PC2): java-spring only -- exactly two records, action 'fetch' then 'patch'. 'recover' has no record of its own: it is governed by the 'fetch' record (HandleController#recover uses requiredAuthority()), though the runtime authorize() call still receives the distinct action string "recover". requiredAuthority/requiredAuthorityForPatch are the legacy scalar PROJECTION of these records; policies is the source of truth.

authorizationMode.description: D-resolver-policy-contract (PC2): java-spring only -- 'delegated' whenever either policies[] record is unresolved. Drives HandleController.java.tmpl's authorizeOrThrow(): 'role' keeps the historical requireAuthority() equality check, 'delegated' skips it and requires an injected AuthorizationPolicy bean instead.
